title: Preserve bar space while the shell restarts
head: 7b0df32b34ca
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Valid theme bar sizes above 256 disconnect the reservation owner
leads.consequence: The theme parser accepts any positive integer for [bar] size-horizontal/size-vertical and the style only applies a minimum of 1. Setting size-horizontal=257 with scale-with-font=false gives the built-in bar a legal 257px cross-axis size, which the sender transmits verbatim. State.parse rejects that snapshot, and the reservation server's reject() clears its previously reserved screens and closes the socket. While the main bar is running it must fall back to its own zone, and across its next crash/restart the independent host no longer reserves the strip. This can also occur through font scaling without an explicit oversized size. Reconcile the producer and protocol ranges or validate/scale before publishing; test the boundary with a production theme size.
leads.triage: factual (Style.qml has no upper clamp; State.js caps 256) verified by coordinator; behavioural consequence confirmed by Opus (run-1 follow-up and run-2 F2); published as the current trigger of F1

leads.summary: Initial connection failures cannot be retried by the new 1-second timer
leads.consequence: If the host socket does not exist or refuses an initial connect (including a connect attempted while a replacement host is still coming up), Quickshell leaves a non-null QLocalSocket in an unconnected state. The timer writes connected=true repeatedly, but Quickshell's setter will not call connectToServer with a non-null socket pointer. The main bar falls back to its own exclusive zone after two seconds and never rejoins a subsequently available host in that shell process. Recreate the Socket object after an error, not merely set connected=false on the failed QLocalSocket; add an absent-then-listening integration test.
leads.triage: in opus final (minor note) and followup-1 Q2; published as F4

leads.summary: A stalled reservation-host directory watcher overrides fresh hidden-bar snapshots
leads.consequence: The host prefers its own flagHidden whenever its initial probe has answered. The 1-second corrective poll only runs during outages (!ready), and omarchy-toggle-bar nudges only the main-shell probe. If the directory watcher misses a rapid toggle while the shell is healthy (the built-in bar already documents that exact failure), the main bar hides or reveals, sends an updated hidden snapshot, but the host ignores it: space remains reserved for a hidden bar or no longer reserved for a visible bar until the host next polls during an outage. Use the fresh owner snapshot while connected and use flag probing only during an outage, or nudge the host on toggles.
leads.triage: in opus final H2; not reproduced as a failure; not published

leads.summary: Restarts from SSH or a TTY cannot announce a deliberate restart to the host
leads.consequence: The restart script explicitly supports callers outside the session, where WAYLAND_DISPLAY can be unset. Its new direct quickshell ipc call runs before any display recovery and lacks --any-display, so Quickshell filters the live reservation instance out as belonging to another display and the error is discarded by || true. The following kill does pass --any-display and the main-shell ping uses the display-recovering omarchy-shell wrapper, so the restart still proceeds but the promised Shell restarting status is never announced. Resolve the Wayland display before the host IPC (prefer the session's display rather than selecting an unrelated display on multi-session systems), or pass an explicitly selected host instance.
leads.triage: in opus final minor note; published as source-only note

leads.summary: The open per-monitor bar filter PR would leave reservations on monitors with no bar
leads.consequence: Open PR #6501 makes the built-in BarPanel Variants use bar.barScreens, honoring user bar.screens=["DP-1". This PR's snapshot instead sends the raw Quickshell.screens names. Once combined, with DP-1 and HDMI-A-1 connected and a bar configured only on DP-1, the reservation process still claims bar-sized exclusive space on HDMI-A-1. Publish the bar's filtered screen set to the host when the filter feature lands, and include the filtered/empty case in integration tests. This is conditional on merging #6501, not a defect in today's unfiltered default. An application of #6501 to a copy of this head applied its Bar.qml and shell.qml hunks; a docs/omarchy-shell.md hunk rejected, so no claim of an entirely clean textual merge.
leads.triage: in opus related PRs; published in Details

leads.summary: Current quattro has an unresolved restart-script merge hunk
leads.consequence: The PR's pre-kill reservation announcement and the current base's pre-kill notifications_ready snapshot both add lines at the same insertion point. A three-way merge produces conflict markers in bin/omarchy-restart-shell at merged lines 64-83. A manual resolution must keep both the reservation announcement and notification readback before the kill; otherwise one feature is silently lost. Other checked overlapping shell/shell.qml, Bar.qml and restart-shell-test.sh files merged without conflict.
leads.triage: in opus F1; published as F3

leads.summary: The launch test's fake daemon can report success without creating a host socket
leads.consequence: The fake -d branch exits 0 after writing its arguments and the socket name; it neither runs shell/bar-reservation/shell.qml nor listens on a socket. A plausible broken launcher or QML host with SocketServer inactive, a rejected path, or a missing handler still passes the added success checks, yet real shells would fail to attach and the bar would cease to be reserved across restarts. Add a command-only localhost/private-socket end-to-end probe in the sandbox that requires an actual successful snapshot acknowledgement, or cover it with a gated compositor fixture. The PR's Node State.js test checks just the library, not the QML host.
leads.triage: corroborates opus mutation results; published within the optional test note

leads.summary: Shell developer instructions still tell users to start a main-only Quickshell process
leads.consequence: The README's direct invocation paragraph claims Hyprland autostart launches `quickshell -p $OMARCHY_PATH/shell`; it actually calls omarchy-launch-shell, which now starts the separate reservation host and exports OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET. A developer following the README to start the shell directly never starts the host, so their bar test cannot exercise persistent reservation. Update shell/README.md:3-6 and 193-201 to name the launcher and the companion while retaining the direct IPC example.

leads.summary: Manual and shell overview retain single-process descriptions of the bar
leads.consequence: Each describes the visible bar as wholly running in the one long-lived shell; this PR introduces a separate resident Quickshell process owning its layer-shell reservation while the interactive bar stays in the main shell. Link docs/bar-reservation.md and qualify each single-process description so users diagnosing orphaned host windows understand why a second Quickshell process appears. These are documentation omissions, not evidence of a runtime failure.
leads.triage: factual check by coordinator: wording still broadly true (plugin host remains single); nitpick; dropped

leads.summary: Open placeholder-screen fixes do not filter the new reservation process
leads.consequence: Open PRs #13645 and #13165 filter Qt's unnamed placeholder and Hyprland FALLBACK output out of all three built-in bar surface lists. This PR still sends the entire Quickshell.screens list and instantiates reservation panels for every screen, including names the new filter deliberately excludes; if the compositor supplies the documented FALLBACK screen with a nonzero size, it can reserve space where no interactive bar exists. The shell tests passed in a synthetic copy combining #13645 and this head, because none asserts that the reservation follows the filter. Needs a disposable-compositor hotplug run to establish the exact visible result on the shipped Qt/Hyprland combination.
leads.triage: depends on unmerged PRs, unconfirmed; dropped

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** A rejected new shell leaves the old reservation mapped beside its own.

### A rejected new shell keeps the old reservation

`reject()` in the host releases the old snapshot only if the rejected connection owns it; after a restart nothing does. **Impact:** the old strip stays, and the new bar adds its own zone and retries each second. In practice this needs a bar over 256 px, or a protocol change the long-lived host rejects.

**Suggested change:** release in `reject()` without an owner, and back off after a rejection.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 7b0df32)</summary>

# Reproducer: a rejected new shell keeps the previous shell's reservation and retries forever

Reviewed head: `7b0df32b34ca48010b66d0f0e8c0cdaae1bc9a5e`. Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2.

`reject()` in `shell/bar-reservation/shell.qml` releases the retained snapshot only when the rejected connection is the current owner. After a restart there is no owner (the previous shell's connection closed), so a new shell whose first snapshot fails `State.parse` is disconnected while the previous shell's reservation stays mapped, with `ready: false` and "Shell restarting…". `BarReservation.qml` then treats the shell as unmanaged (the bar goes back to `ExclusionMode.Auto`) and reconnects every second, and each attempt is rejected the same way. Hyprland arranges bottom-layer exclusive zones before top-layer ones (`arrangeLayersForMonitor`, v0.56.2), so the host's strip and the new bar both reserve space.

Today the rejected snapshot needs a bar thicker than 256 px (`State.parse` caps `size` at 256; `Style.bar.sizeHorizontal` has no upper bound). The same path is taken by any later protocol or validation change, because the host keeps running its old code across main-shell restarts and updates until the next login.

The script runs the PR's host and the PR's unchanged `BarReservation.qml` under Quickshell's offscreen platform, with a private `HOME` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. Offscreen has no layer shell, so the host copy swaps `PanelWindow` for `FloatingWindow` and drops `anchors`, `exclusiveZone` and the `WlrLayershell` properties. The socket, ownership, parsing and visibility code is the PR's text. `surface mapped` is the value of the production `visible:` binding, which decides whether the layer surface, and so its exclusive zone, exists.

Run: `python3 repro_reject_after_restart.py <omarchy checkout at 7b0df32>`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproducer for omacom/omarchy#11887 at 7b0df32.

Runs the PR's reservation host (shell/bar-reservation/shell.qml) and the PR's
BarReservation.qml client under Quickshell's offscreen platform, each with a
private HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Offscreen has no layer shell, so the host
copy swaps PanelWindow for FloatingWindow and drops the three layer-shell-only
properties (anchors, exclusiveZone, WlrLayershell); the socket, ownership,
parsing and visibility code is the PR's text.

1. Shell A connects and reserves the bar (26 px, as the running shell would).
2. omarchy-restart-shell announces the restart; A's connection closes.
3. Shell B (BarReservation.qml, unchanged) connects with a snapshot the host
   rejects: a 300 px bar (State.parse caps size at 256).
4. A raw client sends a future protocol version (version 2).

Usage: python3 repro_reject_after_restart.py <omarchy checkout>
"""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import resource
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

repo = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))
work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='bar-repro-'))
(work / 'run').mkdir(mode=0o700)
(work / 'home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles').mkdir(parents=True)
sock = work / 'bar.sock'
env = dict(PATH=os.environ['PATH'], HOME=str(work / 'home'), XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=str(work / 'run'),
  QT_QPA_PLATFORM='offscreen', QS_DISABLE_CRASH_HANDLER='1', QS_DISABLE_FILE_WATCHER='1',
  QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP='1', OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET=str(sock), LANG='C.UTF-8')
procs = []

host = work / 'host'
host.mkdir()
qml = (repo / 'shell/bar-reservation/shell.qml').read_text()
qml = qml.replace('import Quickshell.Wayland\n', '')
qml = qml.replace('    model: Quickshell.screens\n    delegate: PanelWindow {',
  '    id: surfaces\n    model: Quickshell.screens\n    delegate: FloatingWindow {')
start = qml.index('      anchors {')
qml = qml[:start] + qml[qml.index('      }\n', start) + 8:]
for line in ('      exclusiveZone: root.snapshot.size\n', '      WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Bottom\n',
    '      WlrLayershell.namespace: "omarchy-bar-reservation"\n'):
  assert line in qml
  qml = qml.replace(line, '')
qml = qml.rstrip()[:-1] + '''  IpcHandler {
    target: "repro"
    function mapped(): bool { return surfaces.instances[0].visible }
  }
}
'''
(host / 'shell.qml').write_text(qml)
shutil.copy(repo / 'shell/bar-reservation/State.js', host / 'State.js')

client = work / 'client'
client.mkdir()
shutil.copy(repo / 'shell/services/BarReservation.qml', client / 'BarReservation.qml')
(client / 'shell.qml').write_text('''import QtQuick
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
ShellRoot {
  id: repro
  property var flips: []
  property QtObject fakeBar: QtObject {
    property string position: "top"
    property int barSize: 300
    property bool barHidden: false
    property bool hiddenStateKnown: true
    property color background: "#202020"
    property color foreground: "#ffffff"
  }
  property BarReservation reservation: BarReservation {
    bar: repro.fakeBar; supported: true; contentReady: true
    onManagedChanged: repro.flips = repro.flips.concat([managed])
  }
  IpcHandler {
    target: "repro"
    function state(): string { return JSON.stringify({ managed: repro.reservation.managed, flips: repro.flips }) }
  }
}
''')


def launch(directory):
  process = subprocess.Popen(['quickshell', '-p', str(directory)], env=env,
    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
  procs.append(process)
  return process


def ipc(directory, target, function):
  for _ in range(100):
    result = subprocess.run(['quickshell', 'ipc', '-p', str(directory), 'call', target, function],
      env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode == 0:
      return result.stdout.strip()
    time.sleep(.05)
  raise RuntimeError(result.stderr)


def connect():
  connection = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX)
  connection.settimeout(3)
  connection.connect(str(sock))
  return connection


def frame(**changes):
  value = {'version': 1, 'screens': [''], 'position': 'top', 'size': 26, 'hidden': False,
    'ready': True, 'background': '#111111', 'foreground': '#eeeeee'}  # offscreen screen name is ''
  value.update(changes)
  return (json.dumps(value) + '\n').encode()


def report(step):
  status = json.loads(ipc(host, 'reservation', 'status'))
  print(f'{step}: host ready={status["ready"]} message={status["message"]!r} '
    f'reserved size={status["snapshot"]["size"]} from background={status["snapshot"]["background"]} '
    f'surface mapped={ipc(host, "repro", "mapped")}')


try:
  launch(host)
  ipc(host, 'reservation', 'ping')

  shell_a = connect()
  shell_a.sendall(frame())
  shell_a.recv(8)
  report('1. shell A connected')

  ipc(host, 'reservation', 'restarting')
  shell_a.close()
  time.sleep(.5)
  report('2. restart announced, shell A gone')

  launch(client)
  time.sleep(6)
  state = json.loads(ipc(client, 'repro', 'state'))
  print(f'3. shell B (300 px bar) after 6 s: managed={state["managed"]} managed transitions={state["flips"]}')
  report('3. shell B (300 px bar) after 6 s')

  future = connect()
  future.sendall(frame(version=2))
  reply = future.recv(8)
  future.close()
  time.sleep(.3)
  report(f'4. version 2 client (reply {reply!r})')
finally:
  for process in procs:
    process.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
    process.wait(5)
  shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
```

Actual output:

```
1. shell A connected: host ready=True message='' reserved size=26 from background=#111111 surface mapped=true
2. restart announced, shell A gone: host ready=False message='Shell restarting…' reserved size=26 from background=#111111 surface mapped=true
3. shell B (300 px bar) after 6 s: managed=False managed transitions=[True, False, True, False, True, False, True, False, True, False, True, False]
3. shell B (300 px bar) after 6 s: host ready=False message='Shell restarting…' reserved size=26 from background=#111111 surface mapped=true
4. version 2 client (reply b''): host ready=False message='Shell restarting…' reserved size=26 from background=#111111 surface mapped=true
```

For comparison, the same flow with a 26 px shell B is accepted at once: `managed` becomes true once, the host clears the message, sets `ready: true` and replaces the snapshot with shell B's colors.

</details>

### Without a host, the bar waits 2 s per start

`Quickshell.env()` returns `null` when unset, so `configured` (`BarReservation.qml:10`) stays true after the launcher unsets it; starting a host that fails to load also returns 0. **Impact:** either way the bar stays unmapped for 2 s.

**Suggested change:** use `!!Quickshell.env(...)`, and `ping` the host before exporting the socket.

<details><summary>Reproducer: unset variable (fails at 7b0df32)</summary>

# Reproducer: with OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET unset, the bar still waits 2 s for a reservation host

Reviewed head: `7b0df32b34ca48010b66d0f0e8c0cdaae1bc9a5e`. Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2.

`omarchy-launch-shell` falls back by running `unset OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET` (host start timed out or exited non-zero, or no runtime dir, display or host config). Quickshell 0.3.1's `Quickshell.env()` returns `null` for an unset variable (`src/core/qmlglobal.cpp`, `QuickshellGlobal::env`), and `shell/services/BarReservation.qml:10` tests `Quickshell.env("OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET") !== ""`. Since `null !== ""` is true, `configured` is true without any socket:

- `managed` is false, so the bar keeps `ExclusionMode.Auto`, as intended.
- `waiting` is true until the 2 s `startupExpired` timer fires, because no acknowledgement can arrive. `Bar.qml:1243` therefore keeps the bar unmapped for 2 s on every shell start.
- The one-second retry timer runs for the life of the shell. Each tick sets `connected = true` on a socket whose path is empty, which does nothing.

Before this PR, `Bar.qml` was `visible: !remapGuard.remapping` with `exclusionMode: root.barHidden ? ExclusionMode.Ignore : ExclusionMode.Auto`, so the bar mapped as soon as it was created. The script below runs the PR's unchanged `BarReservation.qml` under Quickshell's offscreen platform with a private `HOME` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. The bar's `visible` and `exclusionMode` expressions are copied from the PR's `Bar.qml` at run time, with `remapGuard.remapping` taken as false.

Run: `python3 repro_unset_socket_env.py <omarchy checkout at 7b0df32>` (both files in one directory).

```python
The host copy swaps PanelWindow for FloatingWindow (offscreen has no layer
shell) and drops anchors, exclusiveZone and the WlrLayershell properties; the
socket, ownership, parsing and visibility code is the PR's text. The client is
the PR's BarReservation.qml, unchanged, next to a stand-in for the built-in bar.
The bar's visible and exclusionMode expressions are copied from the PR's
Bar.qml at run time, with `remapGuard.remapping` taken as false and `root.`

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import resource
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time

resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))


class Lab:
  def __init__(self, repo):
    self.repo = Path(repo).resolve()
    self.work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='bar-repro-'))
    (self.work / 'run').mkdir(mode=0o700)
    (self.work / 'home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles').mkdir(parents=True)
    self.sock = self.work / 'bar.sock'
    self.procs = []
    self.base = dict(PATH=os.environ['PATH'], HOME=str(self.work / 'home'),
      XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=str(self.work / 'run'), QT_QPA_PLATFORM='offscreen',
      QS_DISABLE_CRASH_HANDLER='1', QS_DISABLE_FILE_WATCHER='1', QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP='1', LANG='C.UTF-8')
    self.t0 = time.monotonic()

  def env(self, socket_value='default'):
    env = dict(self.base)
    if socket_value == 'default':
      env['OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET'] = str(self.sock)
    elif socket_value is not None:
      env['OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET'] = socket_value

  def stamp(self):
    return f'[{time.monotonic() - self.t0:5.1f}s]'

    directory = self.work / name
    directory.mkdir()

    qml = qml.replace('    model: Quickshell.screens\n    delegate: PanelWindow {',

      qml = qml.replace(line, '')
    qml = qml.rstrip()[:-1] + '''  IpcHandler {
    target: "repro"
    function mapped(): bool { return surfaces.instances[0].visible }

    (directory / 'shell.qml').write_text(qml)
    shutil.copy(self.repo / 'shell/bar-reservation/State.js', directory / 'State.js')
    return directory

    directory = self.work / name
    directory.mkdir()
    shutil.copy(self.repo / 'shell/services/BarReservation.qml', directory / 'BarReservation.qml')
    bar = (self.repo / 'shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml').read_text()
    match = re.search(r'\n    visible: (!remapGuard\.remapping && [^\n]*)\n'
      r'    exclusionMode: ([^\n]*\n\s*\? ExclusionMode\.Ignore : ExclusionMode\.Auto)\n', bar)

import Quickshell.Io

  property real startedAt: Date.now()
  property real waitingEndedAt: -1
  property int retryTicks: 0
  property var retryTimer: null

    property int barSize: 26
    property bool barHidden: false
    property bool hiddenStateKnown: true

    target: "repro"

    }

''' % (visible, exclusion))
    return directory, visible, exclusion

  # ------------------------------------------------------------ processes
  def launch(self, directory, env):
    process = subprocess.Popen(['quickshell', '-p', str(directory)], env=env,
      stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
    self.procs.append(process)
    return process

  def ipc(self, directory, target, function, env):
    for _ in range(200):
      result = subprocess.run(['quickshell', 'ipc', '-p', str(directory), 'call', target, function],
        env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
      if result.returncode == 0:

    return json.loads(self.ipc(client, 'repro', 'state', env))

    status = json.loads(self.ipc(host, 'reservation', 'status', self.env()))
    return (f'host ready={status["ready"]} message={status["message"]!r} '
      f'snapshot screens={status["snapshot"]["screens"]} size={status["snapshot"]["size"]} '

  def wait(self, predicate, timeout=10):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
      if predicate():
        return True
      time.sleep(.05)
    return False

  def close(self):
    for process in self.procs:
      if process.poll() is None:
        process.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
        process.wait(5)
    shutil.rmtree(self.work, ignore_errors=True)


def short(state, keys):
```

# Reproducer: `quickshell -d -n` reports success for a reservation host that fails to load

Reviewed head: `7b0df32b34ca48010b66d0f0e8c0cdaae1bc9a5e`. Quickshell 0.3.1.

`omarchy-launch-shell` treats a non-zero status from `quickshell -d -n -p …/bar-reservation` as "Bar reservation host unavailable" and unsets `OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET`. In Quickshell 0.3.1 the daemon child exits through `exit(-1)` when its configuration fails to load (`RootWrapper`), without writing to the daemon pipe, so the waiting parent reads end-of-file and returns 0. The launcher then exports a socket nothing listens on, logs nothing, and the main shell's `BarReservation` stays `configured` but unconnected: the bar is hidden for the 2-second startup window on every shell start before it falls back to its own zone. The launcher test models failure with a fake `quickshell` that exits 1, which the real binary does not do for this case.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer for omacom/omarchy#11887 at 7b0df32: `quickshell -d -n` (as
# omarchy-launch-shell starts the reservation host) exits 0 even when the
# configuration fails to load, so the launcher's "Bar reservation host
# unavailable" branch never runs for a broken host. Private HOME and
# XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; offscreen platform; core dumps off.
set -u
ulimit -c 0
t=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -m 700 "$t/run" && mkdir -p "$t/home" "$t/broken"
export HOME=$t/home XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$t/run QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QS_DISABLE_CRASH_HANDLER=1
printf 'import QtQuick\nimport Quickshell\nShellRoot {\n  NoSuchType { }\n}\n' >"$t/broken/shell.qml"
timeout --kill-after=1s 5s quickshell -d -n -p "$t/broken" >/dev/null 2>&1
echo "quickshell -d -n with a config that fails to load: exit status $?"
quickshell list -p "$t/broken" 2>&1 | head -n 1
rm -rf "$t"
```

```
No running instances for "/tmp/tmp.ZYcmt8ncoU/broken/shell.qml"
```

### Conflicts with current `quattro`

`bin/omarchy-restart-shell` conflicts with quattro's pre-kill block (keeping both resolves it). After the merge, `shell-ipc-socket-test.sh` fails, because it allows `IpcHandler {` only in `shell/Commons/IpcRegistry.qml` and `shell/Commons/ShellIpc.qml`.

**Suggested change:** when rebasing, add `shell/bar-reservation/shell.qml` to that list, or exclude `shell/bar-reservation/`, noting that the host deliberately avoids `qs.Commons`.

### A host that returns late is never reconnected

On Quickshell 0.3.1 a failed connect leaves `Socket` holding the dead `QLocalSocket`, so later `connected = true` retries do nothing (fixed upstream after 0.3.1). If the host is not listening at the first retry after a disconnect, the main shell stays on its own zone for the rest of its life, and the next restart moves windows once.

**Suggested change:** recreate the `Socket` object on each retry, for example through a `Loader`.

# Reproducer: a host that comes back after the main shell's first retry is never reconnected, and the next restart loses the reserved space

Reviewed head: `7b0df32b34ca48010b66d0f0e8c0cdaae1bc9a5e`. Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2.

When the host goes away, the main shell's `Socket` gets a disconnect: `onSocketDisconnected` drops the `QLocalSocket`, and does not reconnect because `targetConnected` was cleared when the connection was made (Quickshell 0.3.1 `src/io/socket.cpp:50,56-66`). `BarReservation.qml`'s one-second timer then sets `connected = true`, which starts one new connection attempt (`socket.cpp:83`). If nothing is listening at that moment, the attempt fails and the failed `QLocalSocket` stays in place, so every later tick does nothing (`socket.cpp:68-71,83`). This was fixed upstream after 0.3.1 in commit 41651d7. The main shell stays unmanaged and keeps its own zone for the rest of its life, even after the host returns. The returned host starts with an empty snapshot and `ready: false`. When the main shell is next restarted, nothing is reserved between the old shell's exit and the new shell's first snapshot.

The script runs the PR's host (PanelWindow swapped for FloatingWindow, layer-shell-only properties dropped) and the PR's unchanged `BarReservation.qml` under Quickshell's offscreen platform, with a private `HOME` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. `surface mapped` is the value of the host's production `visible:` binding, which decides whether its layer surface, and so its exclusive zone, exists.

Run: `python3 repro_host_returns_after_retry.py <omarchy checkout at 7b0df32>` (both files in one directory).

```python
  // Stand-in for Bar.qml's root: it reads root.barHidden and root.shell.barReservation.
  property QtObject barRoot: QtObject { property bool barHidden: false; property var shell: harness }
  readonly property bool barVisible: %s
  readonly property int barExclusion: %s
  Component.onCompleted: {
    var r = harness.barReservation.resources
    for (var i = 0; i < r.length; i++) {
      if (("triggeredOnStart" in r[i]) && r[i].interval === 1000 && r[i].repeat) {
        harness.retryTimer = r[i]
        r[i].triggered.connect(function() { harness.retryTicks++ })
      }
    }
  }
  IpcHandler {
    target: "repro"
    function state(): string {
      var s = harness.barReservation
      return JSON.stringify({ elapsedMs: Date.now() - harness.startedAt,
        env: Quickshell.env("OMARCHY_BAR_SOCKET"), configured: s.configured, managed: s.managed,
        waiting: s.waiting, barVisible: harness.barVisible,
        barExclusion: harness.barExclusion === ExclusionMode.Ignore ? "Ignore"
          : harness.barExclusion === ExclusionMode.Auto ? "Auto" : String(harness.barExclusion),
        retryTimerRunning: harness.retryTimer ? harness.retryTimer.running : null,
        retryTicks: harness.retryTicks,
        waitingEndedAfterMs: harness.waitingEndedAt < 0 ? null : harness.waitingEndedAt - harness.startedAt })
    }
  }
}
''' % (visible, exclusion))
    return directory, visible, exclusion

  # ------------------------------------------------------------ processes
  def launch(self, directory, env):
    process = subprocess.Popen(['quickshell', '-p', str(directory)], env=env,
      stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
    self.procs.append(process)
    return process

  def ipc(self, directory, target, function, env):
    for _ in range(200):
      result = subprocess.run(['quickshell', 'ipc', '-p', str(directory), 'call', target, function],
        env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
      if result.returncode == 0:
        return result.stdout.strip()
      time.sleep(.05)
    raise RuntimeError(result.stderr)

  def state(self, client, env):
    return json.loads(self.ipc(client, 'repro', 'state', env))

  def host_view(self, host):
    status = json.loads(self.ipc(host, 'reservation', 'status', self.env()))
    return (f'host ready={status["ready"]} message={status["message"]!r} '
      f'snapshot screens={status["snapshot"]["screens"]} size={status["snapshot"]["size"]} '
      f'surface mapped={self.ipc(host, "repro", "mapped", self.env())}')

  def wait(self, predicate, timeout=10):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
      if predicate():
        return True
      time.sleep(.05)
    return False

  def close(self):
    for process in self.procs:
      if process.poll() is None:
        process.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
        process.wait(5)
    shutil.rmtree(self.work, ignore_errors=True)


def short(state, keys):
  return ' '.join(f'{k}={json.dumps(state[k])}' for k in keys)
```
